subject: memcode
title: Risk classifier and capability denylist walk the same shell AST through one shared unwrapper, with a bypass battery as the standing regression guard
one_why: Reuses the classifier's own innerCommand unwrapper for deny-matching so the risk ladder and the capability ceiling can never disagree about what a command IS (eval/sudo/setsid/parallel with per-wrapper value-flag tables); unparseable input is refused not allowed; direction-based net risk (POST=exfiltration) and RiskHead/RiskSegment anchoring keep remembered-approval patterns covering the highest-risk sub-command.

subject: memcode
title: Hot-raw / warm-summary / cold-session-log tiering with budgets derived from learned lane capacity, never absolute constants
one_why: Every prior magic number (45K, 150K) 'aged into a silent clip' as windows grew 5-20x, so budget = served lane capacity x85% with a window-relative fallback; the warm summarizer is force-escalated because 'a wrong summary silently becomes the session's false memory', and the cold layer's marker tells the model precisely what is retrievable vs must be re-run.

subject: memcode
title: Eviction derived from a measured read-evict-reread thrash: superseded-read dedup (range-aware), decaying hot-path pins, budget-scaled keep counts
one_why: Audit evidence: fixed keep-counts (6/8) were smaller than real working sets, so the same 9 files were re-read 13-14x per session; now an earlier read of a path+range dies the moment it is re-read (a later FULL read covers ranges), paths observed re-read stay pinned with per-turn decay capped at 12, and keep scales 8..32 with budget — offload pointers are typed and lossless ('re-read that range to restore').

subject: memcode
title: Compaction back-off: re-summarize only after >=20% real regrowth, and reserve aggressive keep=2 for the reactive overflow path
one_why: Re-summarizing a history that can't get under budget rewrites the whole prefix each crossing — the measured '3 compactions in 8 minutes' signature — burning a summarizer call and busting the prompt cache for a near-identical result; manual /compact resets the baseline because the user asked.

subject: memcode
title: Stable/volatile system split with 1h doctrine breakpoint, last-tool breakpoint, and clone-only decoration — with a no-mutation property test
one_why: Per-turn volatile facts ride a SEPARATE uncached block after the 1h-cached doctrine so a fact change never busts the prefix; the two-system convention is exported in the public wire protocol (protocol/PROTOCOL.md:14-19); cache_test asserts the caller's structs are untouched, pinning the mutation class of bug that silently rewrites cached bytes.

subject: memcode
title: Repo-shipped .memcode/hooks.json executes through the platform shell at session start with no trust gate
one_why: hooks.Load(root) merges <root>/.memcode/hooks.json and runs commands via the platform shell; no trust/approval check exists anywhere in hooks/config (grep for 'trust' returns nothing) — and .memcode is precisely the team-shared, PR-ed, portable memory directory, so cloning a repo or accepting a PR yields arbitrary code execution before the first prompt.

subject: memcode
title: Scripted fake providers drive real end-to-end turns, and test helpers force every state through production transitions
one_why: The dogfood test exercises the full StartChat->Submit->EndChat pipeline against a scripted provider and asserts the on-disk session log is faithful plus agent self-recall; recordingProv proves which model each delegated worker ran on; enterPlanForTest comments out the whole 'poke private state' cheat: 'raw phase pokes are impossible now, which is the point'.

subject: memcode
title: The product's central claim ships with a counterfactual harness: same task run A/B in isolated git worktrees, context-pack vs cold
one_why: 'Does memcode's state make the agent better?' is measurable in-repo — iterations, tool calls, tokens, files touched, and verification-pass are compared across the two worktree runs; no other subject instruments its own value hypothesis this directly, though (unlike ci.yml:18-36 unit/CI gates) it is never wired into CI.

subject: memcode
title: Unattended agents run under canonical-hashed delegation policies expressed as consequence classes plus hard budgets, expiry, and revocation
one_why: Observe/local_mutation/external_effect/external_representation/financial/legal_attestation/destructive turn permission into a capability vocabulary for standing objectives; MaxActionsPerPeriod/MaxTokens/MaxSeconds/MaxDelegationDepth + ExpiresAt/Revoked, canonicalized (sorted) to a sha256 policy identity; the generated-code runner hard-fails when the hardened sandbox is unavailable instead of downgrading.

subject: memcode
title: Offline MCP stdio server exposes the repo's memory to rival harnesses — switch clients, not agents
one_why: Claude Code/Cursor/Codex users get 'what did we decide about X' / 'where does Y live' from the local .memcode store with no model, no network, and no memcode account; paired with rival-config importers (cmd/migrate.go:23-107 'memcode claw migrate' / 'memcode hermes migrate' bringing channels, keys, skills, and long-term memory), interop is weaponized as a migration funnel.

subject: memcode
title: Deliberately removed the no-progress loop detector; replaced with progress-signature bounding and bounded nudges
one_why: The corpus's only anti-breaker data point: the no-progress stall detector was removed 'for killing legitimate long work'; apply continuations now bound on a todo-STATE fingerprint (real progress resets the counter, spinning terminates), plus bounded heal/stall/leak nudge rounds and iter caps per mode — worth weighing against crush-style repetition breakers when designing ours.

subject: memcode
title: 41.5k-LOC vendored TUI fork copied without recording the upstream version
one_why: 'The exact upstream version it was copied from was not recorded at vendoring time' — no pin, no intent cards, no security-fix path against upstream (contrast kimi-code-2's UPSTREAM.md governance); it also silently inflated census non-test LOC by ~41% for a first-party-looking tree.
